mcqs.learning_point: Using differences in density and settling behaviour
mcqs.question: Which statement best defines why sedimentation and decantation can be used to separate a mixture?

options.A: They depend on the magnetic properties of the components
options.B: They rely on differences in density that cause particles to settle at different rates
options.C: They use heat to evaporate the liquid part of the mixture
options.D: They change the chemical composition of the mixture

mcqs.answer: They rely on differences in density that cause particles to settle at different rates
mcqs.explanation: Sedimentation and decantation work because solid particles that are denser than the liquid settle down faster, creating a clear supernatant that can be poured off. Option B correctly describes this principle, while the other options refer to unrelated processes.

mcqs.question: You have a mixture of sand and water in a beaker. Which method should you use to obtain clear water?

options.B: Decantation after allowing the sand to settle

mcqs.answer: Decantation after allowing the sand to settle
mcqs.explanation: Sand is an insoluble solid that settles at the bottom because it is denser than water. After it settles, the clear water can be poured off (decanted). Distillation and boiling are unnecessary, and adding salt does not separate sand.

mcqs.question: A student tries to separate a mixture of fine flour and water by letting it sit and then decanting the liquid. Why does this method not work well?

options.A: Flour particles are too light to settle quickly

mcqs.answer: Flour particles are too light to settle quickly
mcqs.explanation: Fine flour has a very low density and small particle size, so it remains suspended for a long time and does not settle fast enough for decantation. It does not dissolve, evaporate, or react chemically with water, making options B, C, and D incorrect.

mcqs.question: A jar contains water with a small amount of muddy soil added. After leaving the jar undisturbed for several hours, what will you observe?

options.A: The mud will float on the surface
options.B: The water will turn clear instantly
options.C: The soil particles will settle at the bottom forming a layer of mud
options.D: The mixture will separate into oil and water

mcqs.answer: The soil particles will settle at the bottom forming a layer of mud
mcqs.explanation: Soil particles are denser than water, so over time they settle to the bottom (sedimentation), creating a clear supernatant. They do not float, and there is no oil present. The clearing is gradual, not instant.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about decantation is a common misconception?

options.A: Decantation can separate a solid that has settled from a liquid above it
options.B: Decantation can separate a dissolved salt from water
options.C: Decantation is useful when the solid settles quickly
options.D: Decantation involves carefully pouring off the liquid

mcqs.answer: Decantation can separate a dissolved salt from water
mcqs.explanation: Decantation separates settled solids from liquids; it cannot separate substances that are completely dissolved, such as salt in water. Options A, C, and D correctly describe decantation.

mcqs.learning_point: Using differences in density and settling behaviour
mcqs.question: Two solid pieces are placed in water: Piece X has a density of 2.5 g/cm³ and Piece Y has a density of 0.9 g/cm³. Which piece will settle to the bottom faster and why?

options.A: Piece X, because it is denser than water and experiences a larger downward force
options.B: Piece Y, because lighter objects settle faster
options.C: Both will settle at the same rate because they are in the same liquid
options.D: Neither will settle because water is too viscous

mcqs.answer: Piece X, because it is denser than water and experiences a larger downward force
mcqs.explanation: A denser object experiences a greater net downward force (gravity minus buoyancy) and thus settles more quickly. Piece Y is less dense than water and would tend to float. Options C and D are incorrect because density differences affect settling rate.

mcqs.question: Which method is more suitable for separating a mixture of very fine sand (particle size <0.05 mm) from water, and why?

options.A: Sedimentation, because fine sand settles quickly
options.B: Filtration using a coarse filter paper, because it catches fine particles
options.C: Sedimentation followed by decantation, because fine sand settles slowly and needs time
options.D: Centrifugation, because it is the only method that works for fine particles

mcqs.answer: Sedimentation followed by decantation, because fine sand settles slowly and needs time
mcqs.explanation: Very fine sand settles very slowly, so allowing sufficient time for sedimentation and then decanting the clear water is the practical approach in a classroom setting. Simple filtration may clog, and centrifugation is not part of the syllabus. Option A is wrong because fine sand does not settle quickly.

mcqs.question: Which statement about sedimentation and decantation is NOT true?

options.A: They cannot separate mixtures where the solid particles are too fine to settle appreciably
options.B: They are ineffective when the solid and liquid have similar densities
options.C: They can be used to separate a dissolved sugar solution from water
options.D: They require the solid to be insoluble in the liquid

mcqs.answer: They can be used to separate a dissolved sugar solution from water
mcqs.explanation: Sedimentation and decantation work only for insoluble solids that settle. A dissolved sugar solution cannot be separated by these methods, making option C false. The other statements correctly describe limitations.
